paragraphs: Amilia sells software that pulls memberships, program registration, payments, and reporting into one system. The customer it describes is the community organization that runs classes, memberships, and facilities for local families.

Registration happens through a branded online store that can stand on its own or sit inside the organization's existing website. Age or skill restrictions and defined registration periods control who can sign up for which activity. Waitlists fill open spots as soon as a registration is cancelled. On the facilities side, a calendar keeps bookings, activities, and rental contracts in sync so staff can see which space is in use and when. Access rules decide which memberships, activities, or passes open the door at each entry point.
The company states that over 1,500 organizations have chosen it. It advertises a 99.99% uptime guarantee for round-the-clock selling. Help is offered by live chat, phone, and email.
